title: Explicit-Formula Translation Between Primes and Zeros
shared_structure: A transform-based dictionary converts weighted prime data into zero data and back, so a statement on one side acquires a translated form on the other.
synthesis: Riemann builds the bridge by replacing prime-power terms inside log zeta with Mellin-type integrals and then inverting to recover the weighted prime-counting function from a contour integral. Bombieri recasts the same bridge as Weil's explicit formula for test functions, where transformed values at 0, 1, and the nontrivial zeros balance a prime-power sum and local terms, and in function fields the identity becomes a Lefschetz trace formula. AIM then uses that prime-zero duality as the reason prime-counting error terms and zero-location statements can be listed as equivalent formulations of RH.
limits: The shared structure is a translation device, not a simplification theorem: once the dictionary is fixed, one still has to control the oscillatory zero side or the prime-side error term. Bombieri's trace interpretation is strongest in the function-field setting, and AIM's equivalence map is survey-level rather than a new proof route.
historical_change: The viewpoint shifts from Riemann's single inversion formula for a weighted prime count to Weil/Bombieri's test-function trace dictionary, where the same prime-zero duality is organized as a local/global identity.
candidate_quality_note: High-confidence candidate: all three units explicitly state the prime-zero duality and make the remaining proof burden visible.

title: Equivalent Criteria Repackage Rather Than Solve RH
shared_structure: An equivalent criterion replaces zero locations by an inequality, closure problem, or positivity statement while preserving the full logical difficulty of RH.
synthesis: Lagarias turns RH into the elementary-looking divisor-sum inequality of Problem E, but says directly that the hard work still sits inside Robin's deeper criterion. Baez-Duarte likewise strengthens Nyman-Beurling by asking for chi to lie in the thinner natural-number closure subspace B_nat, so the representation changes from zeros to Hilbert-space approximation without removing the closure burden. Conrey then reframes Weil's explicit formula as positivity, first for admissible test functions and then for Li's discrete sequence, while openly noting that the source still lacks an interpretation that makes positivity feel natural rather than merely equivalent.
limits: These units genuinely share relocation of difficulty, not ease of proof. The Lagarias and Baez-Duarte criteria remain global all-n or all-approximant statements, and Conrey's positivity formulation is explicit about its interpretive gap.
historical_change: The criterion language moves from arithmetic inequalities to functional positivity and Hilbert-space closure, but the shift is representational rather than an escape from RH's hardness.
candidate_quality_note: Strong candidate: the units are overtly about equivalence and each names the place where difficulty reappears.

title: Random-Matrix Transfer of Local Zero Statistics
shared_structure: Short-range zero statistics are probed by Fourier/test-function machinery and then transferred to unitary random-matrix statistics after matching the mean spacing scale.
synthesis: Montgomery's theorem studies differences of zero ordinates through a weighted Fourier transform F(alpha,T) and proves the random-matrix-looking behavior only on the restricted range 0 <= alpha < 1. His conjectural extension and Dyson's observation then select the unitary/Hermitian symmetry class and reject real-symmetric and symplectic alternatives. Keating and Snaith take that transfer seriously enough to model value distributions of zeta by CUE characteristic polynomials, fixing matrix size by N = log(T/2pi) and then separating the finite-height story into a universal random-matrix part plus an arithmetic correction expressible through primes.
limits: The common structure is statistical transfer, not an exact identification of zeta with a matrix model. Montgomery's proved range is limited, and Keating-Snaith explicitly keep finite-height prime corrections separate from the universal CUE term.
historical_change: The viewpoint changes from a conditional probe of zero spacings to a systematic program that imports random-matrix calculations for zeta values after a scale-matching step.
candidate_quality_note: High-confidence candidate: the units line up tightly on scale matching, model selection, and the need to keep arithmetic corrections visible.

title: Finite Verification Needs Completeness, Not Just Computation
shared_structure: Computational evidence about zeros becomes mathematically meaningful only when local sign information is paired with a completeness argument, and even then its reach is finite.
synthesis: The 1956 computation uses Gram intervals and follow-up subdivision to diagnose failures of Gram's Law, showing that raw machine output can reveal interesting local behavior without yet guaranteeing the full zero count. Platt and Trudgian make the missing requirement explicit: sign changes on the critical line are combined with rigorous truncation control, ball arithmetic, and a Turing-style completeness check so one can certify that all expected zeros in a height range have been found. Their downstream section then shows what this finite certification immediately buys on prime-counting and zero-free estimates, while also recording that some improvements are only slight.
limits: This synthesis stops at finite-height certification. Even the rigorous modern result proves RH only up to a stated height and improves several explicit corollaries only within corresponding bounded ranges or by meagre amounts.
historical_change: The viewpoint moves from exploratory machine detection of sign-pattern failures and ad hoc local rechecks to reproducible interval-certified verification with an explicit completeness layer and explicit finite reach.
candidate_quality_note: Strong candidate: the sources explicitly distinguish local computation, rigorous certification, and the bounded inferential reach of finite verification.

title: L-Function Families Turn Single Objects into Symmetry Classes
shared_structure: Hard single-object behavior is transferred to a family or global geometric setting where local factors or low-lying zeros can be organized by cohomology or symmetry type.
synthesis: Bombieri's function-field discussion shows how a zeta function becomes a geometric object whose zeros and poles are interpreted as Frobenius eigenvalues on cohomology, so local divisor data enters a global topological package. Rubinstein's one-level-density setup likewise replaces one L-function by a conductor-ordered family and studies scaled zeros near 1/2 through an averaged density D(F,phi), expecting a limit governed by an orthogonal or symplectic symmetry class. Miller's symplectic test then compares the number-theoretic lower-order terms of a family average to the Ratios Conjecture prediction, again treating family averaging as the route by which delicate zero behavior becomes structurally legible.
limits: Bombieri is explicit that the finite-field case is evidence and analogy for classical RH, not a transfer theorem back to zeta. The family-density sources remain averaged statements with support restrictions and conjectural ingredients, so they do not yield pointwise control of one selected L-function.
historical_change: The viewpoint changes from the geometry of a single function-field zeta function to large L-function families whose low-lying zeros are classified by a symmetry law rather than by direct inspection one function at a time.
candidate_quality_note: Moderately strong candidate: the family/global move is explicit in all three units, though Bombieri's role is analogical rather than a direct family theorem.

title: Physical and Spectral Re-encodings of Zeta
shared_structure: A physical or spectral representation tries to encode zeta in another observable so that zero information appears as spectrum, overlap amplitude, or phase condition rather than as direct analysis of the Dirichlet series.
synthesis: Connes recasts the zeros as an absorption spectrum on adele-class spaces and shows that the local trace formulas recover exactly the local Weil-explicit-formula terms, while the missing global trace formula would be equivalent to RH for Groessencharakter L-functions. The entanglement/analytic-continuation unit realizes the Dirichlet representation as an overlap amplitude of a time-evolved zeta state, translating convergence into a physical conservation law. The Veneziano unit goes further in criterion form, dressing a scattering amplitude so that an explicit integral condition on its argument becomes equivalent to RH.
limits: These are not the same in strength: Connes presents an open spectral program, the zeta-state construction only realizes the Dirichlet side and explicitly stops at the sigma = 1 wall, and the Veneziano statement is an exact reformulation rather than an independent physical derivation. What is shared is the representational move, not a common completed proof strategy.
historical_change: The viewpoint evolves from an abstract spectral program on adele-class spaces to more concrete quantum or string-theoretic encodings that make the representation vivid while leaving decisive analytic obligations elsewhere.
candidate_quality_note: Moderate-confidence candidate: the re-encoding theme is genuine, but the units differ sharply in whether they offer a program, a realization, or a criterion.

title: Auxiliary Weights Become the Real Optimization Problem
shared_structure: Instead of attacking zeta directly, one engineers weighted auxiliary Dirichlet-polynomial objects whose length, coefficients, or multiplicity are tuned to expose the desired averaged signal.
synthesis: Conrey's two units make this explicit for critical-line zeros: the longer mollifier only works because analytic reduction, arithmetic main-term asymptotics, and Kloosterman-sum error control are imported together, and the coefficient b(n,P) together with the derivative combination sum a_n(s) zeta^(n)(s) is deliberately left tunable until the end. Bui's later critical-zero paper shows that extending the surrogate to several mollifier pieces does not just add flexibility but creates fresh admissibility obligations, enough that one claimed choice is called doubtful and corrected. Harper's moment bound pushes the same indirect philosophy on the value side by replacing one Dirichlet polynomial with many jointly controlled ones in order to recover the sharp conditional moment size.
limits: The shared structure is optimization of a surrogate, not a single uniform method. Longer or more numerous auxiliary pieces only help when the corresponding twisted moments or error terms can actually be controlled, and Harper's theorem remains RH-conditional.
historical_change: The viewpoint shifts from one carefully optimized mollifier in Levinson-style zero counting to broader families of auxiliary polynomials, where the central question becomes which tuned surrogate is analytically admissible.
candidate_quality_note: Good candidate with some scope risk: the common mechanism is clear, but the units mix zero-proportion and moment problems rather than one theorem family.

title: Partial Results by Excluding or Diluting Bad Zeros
shared_structure: When RH is out of reach, one still obtains leverage by proving that too many zeros cannot enter certain regions, or that no zero enters an explicitly bounded region near sigma = 1.
synthesis: Jutila's zero-density unit counts how often relevant Dirichlet polynomials can be large and converts that frequency information into bounds for how many L-function zeros can occupy a rectangle. The 2000 explicit zero-free-region unit instead turns Vinogradov-Korobov-type growth bounds for zeta into a concrete forbidden region near sigma = 1. The 2024 comparison paper keeps the same aim but makes the method modular: different trigonometric polynomials, improved growth bounds, verified RH heights, and intermediate splicing are combined to widen the best region at different height scales.
limits: These sources share a partial-result mechanism, not a route to the critical line. Density estimates and zero-free regions both quantify exclusion near the edge of the strip, and the modern explicit improvements are highly sensitive to constants, height ranges, and auxiliary optimization choices.
historical_change: The viewpoint moves from counting bad zeros by large-value frequency to splicing several explicit zero-free mechanisms, including computational input, into a height-dependent exclusion package.
candidate_quality_note: High-confidence candidate: the region-exclusion logic is explicit in all three units and the historical refinement is concrete rather than stylistic.

title: Heat Flow Turns Zero Statistics into an Obstruction
shared_structure: A deformation in t evolves zero configurations until statistical behavior becomes the contradiction mechanism, so zero statistics act as a boundary condition on a dynamical flow.
synthesis: Rodgers and Tao embed RH into the backward-heat-flow family H_t and isolate the threshold Lambda separating real-zero and non-real-zero regimes. Their proof-strategy unit then says that if Lambda were negative, repulsion and energy monotonicity would drive the zeros of H_0 toward local arithmetic-progression equilibrium. Montgomery's pair-correlation unit supplies the incompatible comparison object: the zero statistics selected by the zeta function are unitary-type and not the locally rigid arithmetic-spacing pattern that the negative-Lambda flow would force.
limits: The contradiction is not produced by heat flow alone. It depends on importing existing statistical information about zeta zeros, so the heat-flow viewpoint relocates the proof burden to dynamical control plus an external non-equilibrium input.
historical_change: A statistic first introduced as a conjectural description of zero spacings is repurposed as the obstruction that rules out an entire deformation scenario for the zeros.
candidate_quality_note: Strong candidate: the Rodgers-Tao unit explicitly names Montgomery-type local statistics as the final contradiction, so the cross-source dependency is direct.

title: Almost-Everywhere Control Replaces Pointwise Ambition
shared_structure: Instead of insisting on uniform pointwise behavior, one measures how often a phenomenon occurs, allowing exceptional sets or probabilistic limits while retaining meaningful structure.
synthesis: Gallagher shows that under RH the prime-number-theorem remainder can be sharpened except on a set of finite logarithmic measure, and more generally that almost-all statements follow from mean-square control. The generalized-almost-periodicity unit does something parallel for zeta values: mean motions and relative zero frequencies for log zeta(s)-x and zeta(s)-x exist in strips, so one studies distribution across vertical lines rather than one exceptional ordinate at a time. The mesoscopic fluctuation theorem pushes this further by giving a Gaussian limit law with covariance determined by relative shift scales, again summarizing typical behavior rather than pointwise exactness.
limits: What is shared is a controlled weakening of the target. Exceptional-set bounds, mean motions, and mesoscopic Gaussian limits do not by themselves recover a uniform pointwise statement about every x or every t.
historical_change: The viewpoint changes from conditional almost-all prime-counting control to a broader distributional language in which zeta values and zeros are described by frequencies, convex Jensen functions, and mesoscopic Gaussian laws.
candidate_quality_note: Good candidate: the units all trade pointwise control for measure or law, though they do so for different observables.

title: From Analytic Inversion to Statistical and Spectral Viewpoints
shared_structure: Each source changes representation in order to expose regularity that the previous representation hid, but the kind of regularity sought changes from exact reconstruction to statistical law to spectral trace.
synthesis: Riemann uses Mellin/Fourier inversion to pass from Euler-product data to a weighted prime-counting function, so the main ambition is exact analytic reconstruction. Montgomery leaves exact reconstruction in the background and instead studies the statistics of zero differences, extracting a pair-correlation law that can be matched to a unitary spectral ensemble. Connes changes the target again, treating the zeros as an absorption spectrum on adele-class spaces and making a global trace formula, rather than a direct explicit inversion, the decisive missing object.
limits: This is a genuine historical change in viewpoint, not a single reusable theorem. The later representations gain access to new regularities, but they also lose some of the direct prime-counting content of Riemann's setup and require new external inputs or missing trace identities.
historical_change: The representation of arithmetic irregularity moves from contour inversion, to statistical spacing laws, to a cohomological/spectral trace problem on adele-class spaces.
candidate_quality_note: Strong historical synthesis candidate: the sources do not merely differ by date, they overtly change what kind of structure is being extracted from the same arithmetic object.

title: When Attractive Representations Lose the Decisive Step
shared_structure: An appealing auxiliary representation can preserve some structural resemblance to RH while failing exactly at the point where decisive mathematical control is needed.
synthesis: AIM's failure catalogue is the cleanest version: Turan-type zero-free conditions for partial sums and de Branges-type positivity conditions both imply RH, but the proposed auxiliary statements are themselves false. Conrey's spectral anecdote shows a softer failure mode, where computed Laplacian eigenvalues seemed to contain zeta-zero ordinates until the data were traced to pseudo cusp forms and computational artefact. Connes's periodic-orbit comparison keeps the analogy alive only as a constraint list, because the sign and finite-repeat mismatches show that the semiclassical picture does not yet carry the exact arithmetic burden of the Euler product.
limits: These are not all failures of the same severity: some routes are falsified, others are merely incomplete or artefactual. The common lesson is narrower and more useful than 'physics fails': a representation is only informative if the exact sign, symmetry, or positivity obligations survive the translation.
historical_change: The failure mode shifts from outright false sufficient conditions to later analogy stress tests that preserve some diagnostic value while discarding literal proof claims.
candidate_quality_note: High-confidence candidate: every unit is explicitly about an attractive route that breaks at a concrete, named mismatch or falsified premise.
